intro: Acute care nurses bring strong judgment, coordination and patient care, skills that transfer across health care. The closest of the 25 careers below is Paramedics, with an 87% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $60,600, so most close moves keep the clinical work but pay less.
why_it_works: On a busy unit you assess unstable patients, coordinate with doctors and calm families at the same time. O*NET rates service orientation at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, and coordination, judgment and social perceptiveness at 4. BLS reports acute care nurses only as part of the registered nurse group, so this page lists medians instead of percent changes. Teaching and counseling roles pay more but need graduate study.
tips: Before leaving nursing, look at outpatient, education or case management roles that use your license.
Health specialties teachers earn $107,310 but usually need a graduate degree.
Medical equipment and informatics roles suit you if you like technology, since equipment and programming are your gaps.

faq.q: What jobs can former acute care nurses do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Paramedics (87%), licensed practical nurses (86%) and Nursing Assistants (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Physical Therapist Assistants are also 76% matched, with a median of $68,380, and need an associate degree rather than a nursing license.

faq.q: Which jobs for acute care nurses pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are postsecondary health specialties teachers at $107,310, Genetic Counselors at $100,040 and Coroners at $80,730, according to BLS May 2025 data. BLS reports acute care nurses within the registered nurse group, so compare these with your own pay.

faq.q: Do acute care nurses need another degree to switch?
faq.a: For most matches, no. 20 of the 25 need no more education than acute care nurses already have, but 5 usually need a graduate degree, including college teaching and genetic counseling. Many roles in this group expect a professional certification as well.

faq.q: What skills should acute care nurses build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, repairing, programming and instructing. Judgment and coordination already rate 4 out of 5 for acute care nurses in O*NET, so technical and teaching skills are the main steps outside bedside care.
